claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in HEA multilayer coatings is governed by multilayer interfaces acting as dislocation barriers.
Multilayer interfaces can be treated as analogous to twist grain boundaries.
The interfaces impede the nucleation of partial dislocations.
The interfaces impede transmission or propagation of partial dislocations.
Impeded partial-dislocation nucleation and transmission slows creep deformation.
The example material has an equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi composition.
The proposed coating contains well-defined alternating layers with twist-misoriented interfaces.
Elevated-temperature constant-load or cyclic loading activates time-dependent deformation in the proposed coatings.
Twist grain boundaries in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can act as nucleation sites for partial dislocations under tensile loading.
After nucleation, multilayer interfaces act as barriers to propagation of the partial dislocations.
Multilayer interfaces pin and distribute partial dislocations.
Dislocation pinning at interfaces inhibits the growth of deformation zones and produces a more uniform strain distribution.
The interface-mediated mechanism reduces creep rate relative to monolithic coatings of similar composition.
Multilayer coatings will have a lower creep strain rate than monolithic HEA coatings.
Multilayer coatings will exhibit localized partial dislocations near their interfaces.
Multilayer coatings will exhibit a more uniform dislocation structure than monolithic coatings.
The proposed mechanism operates when individual layers are sufficiently thin for interface effects to dominate bulk deformation.
The mechanism applies only in a temperature and stress regime where creep is active without phase transformations or competing mechanisms.
Grain-boundary studies in HEAs support dislocation hindrance by interfaces.
The quantitative contribution of multilayer interfaces may vary with microstructural heterogeneity and interface quality.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says interfaces impede partial-dislocation nucleation, whereas the structural mediator describes the same interfaces as sites for partial-dislocation nucleation.
